subject: Priority on-call rotation & cost-sharing for premium SLA
messages:
From: Alex Porter <alex.porter@brightcart.com>
To: Rohan Mehta <rohan.mehta@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-05-11T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Premium SLA: priority rotation cost and overnight coverage

Hi Rohan,

Thanks for the earlier demo — BrightCart is very interested in Redwood's Dedicated offering, but procurement is asking for a tighter definition of the premium support package. Specifically, they want:

- Pricing for a "priority" on-call rotation (primary contact for P1s) that covers US business hours and an optional overnight/weekend rotation.
- How costs would be shared if BrightCart chooses to have a single primary rotation across three product teams (payments, storefront, analytics).
- Any discounts tied to a 12-month commit vs month-to-month.

Can you send a short proposal or ballpark numbers? Procurement is already on standby (procurement@brightcart.com). If it helps, we can book 30 minutes next week to walk through a cost split.

Thanks,
Alex
Alex Porter
Head of Infrastructure
BrightCart

From: Rohan Mehta <rohan.mehta@redwood.com>
To: Alex Porter <alex.porter@brightcart.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-05-11T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Premium SLA: priority rotation cost and overnight coverage

Alex — thanks for the note, and great to hear BrightCart is moving quickly.

High-level: we can offer a modular premium SLA that separates (1) a base retainer for 24x7 P1 coverage (or business-hours only), (2) an on-call rotation surcharge (applied when staff are paged outside business hours), and (3) per-incident credits/offsets for missed SLAs. For multi-team setups we recommend a shared primary rotation with costs apportioned by usage (percent of incidents originating from each team) or equally if you want a simple split.

Marissa / Ben — looping you in to help put numbers together. Marissa, can you model (a) business-hours primary only, (b) business-hours + limited weekend rotation, and (c) full 24x7 primary rotation? Include a 10%/15%/20% discount tier for annual commits at $250k/$500k/$1M respectively. Also flag any operational constraints (on-call headcount, escalation windows).

Alex — I'll circle back early next week with a short worksheet and a proposed PO-ready SLA doc. If procurement wants a quick call, I'm available Tue/Wed.

—Rohan
Rohan Mehta
Director, Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference

From: Rohan Mehta <rohan.mehta@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-05-12T08:32:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: cost model inputs for BrightCart (BRG-4127)

Marissa / Ben —

Quick notes for the worksheet:

1) Proposed components
   - Base retainer: covers priority routing, runbook maintenance, and up to X dedicated hours/month of triage.
   - Rotation surcharge: per-person monthly cost when we staff a named primary during nights/weekends.
   - Incident credits: tokenized credits used to offset penalties if we miss agreed uptime windows; these scale with severity.

2) Charging approach options
   - Usage-proportional: split rotation surcharge by % of incidents per product team (accurate but requires instrumentation).
   - Equal-split: simple, 1/3 each for payments/storefront/analytics.
   - Headcount-share: allocate based on number of owners on BrightCart side who will be primary contacts.

3) Discount levers
   - Annual commit (12 mo) — suggested 10% at $250k, 15% at $500k, 20% at $1M+.
   - Pilot: 3-month pilot at a 5% pilot discount, with full pricing on renewal.

4) SLA mechanics to propose
   - P1: 15-minute acknowledgement during business hours, 30-minute acknowledgement 24x7 (if 24x7 selected); P1 resolution target: 4 hours for critical P1s.
   - P2: business-hours acknowledgement within 1 hour.

Can you run numbers for the three rotation options (BH-only, BH+limited weekend, 24x7) and include an amortized per-month cost and an annual committed price with the discount tiers above? Attachments: please include a simple XLSX with the cost split and a one-page customer-facing summary.

Thanks —R

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Rohan Mehta <rohan.mehta@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-05-14T14:20:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Internal: cost model inputs for BrightCart (BRG-4127)

Rohan — attached is a draft cost split (BRG_cost_split.xlsx). High level:

- Business-hours primary only (shared across 3 teams, equal split): $9,500/mo total (so ~$3,167 per team).
- Business-hours + limited weekend coverage (weekend on-call escalation up to 2 hours): $13,200/mo total (~$4,400 per team).
- Full 24x7 named primary rotation: $21,000/mo total (~$7,000 per team).

Discounted annual pricing (applied to total):
- $250k commit -> 10% off (roughly 1.2 months free)
- $500k commit -> 15% off
- $1M+ commit -> 20% off

Pilot suggestion: 3-month pilot of the BH+limited weekend package at a 7% pilot discount, then convert to annual pricing with a 12-month commit if BrightCart wants a deeper discount.

Notes: the rotation surcharge assumes 2 FTEs in the named rotation to hit our 24x7 SLAs without excessive burnout; that drives the steepness of the 24x7 price. The incident-credit pool we proposed is 10 credits/month for the BH package, 20 credits/month for BH+weekend, 40 credits/month for 24x7. Credits redeemable per missed SLA or escalated postmortem requirement.

Attachment: BRG_cost_split.xlsx (spreadsheet)

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Pricing Manager
Redwood Inference

From: Rohan Mehta <rohan.mehta@redwood.com>
To: Alex Porter <alex.porter@brightcart.com>
Cc: procurement@brightcart.com, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-05-16T10:45:00-07:00
Subject: Proposed SLA and pilot pricing for BrightCart (BRG-4127)

Alex —

Thanks for the patience. Attached is a short, PO-ready proposal (BRG-SLA-Proposal-v1.pdf) plus the cost split worksheet. TL;DR options below:

1) Business-hours primary (equal split across product teams): $9,500/mo total.
2) Business-hours + limited weekend escalation: $13,200/mo total. Recommended pilot configuration: BH+limited weekend for 3 months at a 7% pilot discount.
3) Full 24x7 named primary rotation: $21,000/mo total.

Discounts: Annual commit tiers are available (10%/15%/20% at $250k/$500k/$1M). We can apply an additional 2% discount if BrightCart signs within 30 days of the pilot end.

Operational terms: we maintain a shared primary rotation and provide runbooks, on-call handoff notes, and weekly triage syncs during the pilot. We will provide an escalation matrix and meet SOC 2 requirements (reporting / audit logs available on request).

Requested next steps:
- If this looks good, procurement can send a PO to contracts@redwood.com or we can generate a DocuSign for signature.
- If you want usage-proportional splitting, we can instrument incident attribution during the pilot and finalize the split at pilot close.

Attaching: BRG-SLA-Proposal-v1.pdf (proposal), BRG_cost_split.xlsx (worksheet).

Best,
Rohan

From: Alex Porter <alex.porter@brightcart.com>
To: Rohan Mehta <rohan.mehta@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@brightcart.com
Date: 2025-05-20T15:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Proposed SLA and pilot pricing for BrightCart (BRG-4127)

Rohan —

Thanks for the clear breakdown. BrightCart is happy to proceed with the 3-month pilot (BH+limited weekend) at the 7% pilot discount. Procurement will do a quick legal review and then we can sign a PO. A few asks from our side:

- Can you send a final quote with yearly amortized price and a DocuSign link?
- Please include the incident credit definitions (what constitutes a redeemable missed SLA) in the doc we sign.
- Procurement prefers net-45 payment terms; will Redwood accept net-45 on the pilot PO?

If you can get that over by EOW, procurement will aim to issue the PO early next week.

Appreciate the responsiveness —Alex
Alex Porter
Head of Infrastructure
BrightCart
